sacculārius, sacculāriī m.

noun, second declension · Declension on Wiktionary

cut-purse, pickpocket

From sacculus, a money bag: one who steals from purses by sleight of hand (Lewis & Short). In Asconius, Cicero’s first-century commentator, and in the legal texts.

Other words

  • manticulor, manticulārī — pick pockets, steal

    verb, first conjugation, deponent · also used · post-classical · Apul. Mag. 55 (Lewis & Short); Traupman 359 · Conjugation on Wiktionary

    “To be busy with purses”; ante- and post-classical (Lewis & Short).

  • levātor, levātōris m. — thief (“lifter”)

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Petr. 140 (doubtful reading; Lewis & Short); Traupman 359 · Declension on Wiktionary

See also thief, steal.
